title: A room with no doorway is accepted, counted, and dead — and the one sentence a player gets says "Walled in on every side" whether or not anyone can get in
body:
Found by playing (`playtest/is-there-anything-to-do`). **This closes an open question I raised myself in #933 and flagged there as UNVERIFIED.** I wrote that whether a prisoner can reach a bed in a fully-walled room *"is a pathfinding question I did not test"*, and that if they cannot, *"a door is needed in practice while being absent from the requirement list — which would make this issue worse rather than better."*

**It is worse. Measured, with a refuting sample that survived.**

Every citation below I opened myself on `main`.

## 1. The measurement

**Without a door.** A 3×3 shower room at (19,15)–(21,17), 12 wall segments, **designated and accepted on attempt 1**, two `shower-head-brick` orders each submitting one command. Four prisoners already at `Hygiene 8–11%` after four days in the standing cell.

- Of **21 published counts, exactly one a player can see moved: `ROOMS` 1→2.**
- Two days later: **`Hygiene 0%` on all four prisoners.**
- Across **five acts, not one room-targeted action ever appeared** on the roster.

**With a door — the refuting sample, replicated in three runs.** The same prison, one wooden door per room (cell walled except `18,14 west`, shower except `19,16 west`):

- **`Hygiene` 98% / 100% / 96%** at day +4,
- roster showing **`Showering`** and **`Heading to Showering`**.

Same build, same geometry, one edge different. **The claim survived its refutation attempt.**

## 2. Why — and the code says it in its own words

**Traversal requires a *registered door*, not merely a gap.** `src/simulation/navigation/traversal.ts:23-36`:

> **a registered door decides the edge, whatever value the edge layer holds.** That is not a convention, it is the only reason a doorway is not a wall … **any non-zero value with no registered door is an impassable wall**

**And enclosure already knows it can no longer tell the two apart.** `src/simulation/rooms/enclosure.ts:70-78`:

> A completed door order now writes `DOOR_EDGE_NUMERIC_ID` into the same layer *and* registers a `DoorDefinition`, so this function reports a room with a door in its wall line as `'sealed'` — correctly, because it is: the perimeter really is closed, and the way in is a gated crossing that only navigation can see … **So a `'sealed'` answer no longer implies "no way in"**, and an `'open'` one still means exactly what it says.

That paragraph is precise and honest about the simulation. **The problem is that `'sealed'` is the only thing the player is told**, and the string is:

```ts
// src/content/default-locale-en.ts:1792
'hud.rooms.enclosure-sealed': 'Walled in on every side',
```

**Identical in the working prison and the dead one.** It is not a false sentence about geometry — the perimeter really is closed in both. It is the only signal a player gets, and it cannot distinguish a room that works from a room nobody can enter.

**And the panel's only completion warning fires on a missing *object*, never on a missing way in** — `src/ui/simulation-room-needs.ts:101-111`. So a shower room with both shower heads placed and no doorway reports **complete**.

## 3. The diagnostic for exactly this state exists and is published to nobody

`src/simulation/prisoners/action-system.ts:104-110` — `ActionMetrics.unmetDemandCycles`:

> cycles where no legal action had a reachable, available target

**That is a literal description of the defect state**, computed every cycle, and it reaches no surface: zero hits in `src/ui/`, `src/main.ts`, `src/rendering/` or `src/simulation/presentation/`.

It is a **new** orphan, not one #918's census already held: it appears in **none** of the three sets that census enumerates (projection ids, `statusCountsSchema` fields, presentation view-model members) **because it has no projection at all**. The agent checked it against that note before claiming it, which is the right order.

## 4. Why this is severe rather than a polish item

A player who builds their second room correctly in every way the game checks gets:

- a room the game **accepts**,
- a badge that **counts** it,
- a requirements block that reports it **complete**,
- a sentence saying it is **walled in on every side**,
- and **nothing ever uses it**, while the need it was built for falls to zero.

**There is no refusal, no warning, no band, and no number that moves.** This is the shape of defect the project's own standing directive is aimed at — *"gra ma być łatwa przyjazna do grania, a nie jakieś ukryte funkcje"* — and it breaks the loop the mid-game consists of (build the rooms that change what prisoners do), silently, at the second room.

**It is not the same as #933.** #933 is that the *instruction* names one of four requirements. This is that the *requirement list itself* is missing the thing that makes a room function, and every readout confirms success.

## 5. A sibling defect found in the same run, recorded here because the fix interacts

**Room requirements are advisory at designation time.** A `room.cell` at (19,11)–(21,14) with **zero beds and zero toilets** was accepted on attempt 1 and took `ROOMS` 1→2. And objects can only be placed *inside* an already-zoned room — so `NEEDS 1 × BED` **can never be satisfied at designation time**, by construction. Whatever fix lands here must not assume requirements are checked at zoning, because they are not.

## 6. The candidate fixes, and the choice is real

1. **Make reachability a requirement.** Add a requirement type — the vocabulary is closed at `src/simulation/rooms/definition.ts:4` (`'minimum-size' | 'enclosed' | 'object' | 'outdoors'`), so this is a **protocol and catalogue change**, and per §5 it cannot be enforced at designation time the way the object requirements are not. It would have to be a *completion* check, like the room-needs readout.
2. **Say it in the room-needs readout.** Cheapest and honest: the readout already exists and already reports incompleteness; it currently only counts objects. *"No way in"* is a computable fact — `buildNavigationGraph` reads `DoorRegistry` before the edge value, so the answer is available where the readout is built.
3. **Publish `unmetDemandCycles`.** Does not prevent the mistake but makes it visible after the fact, and it is the diagnostic already written for it. Weakest alone, strongest as a companion.
4. **Change the sentence.** *"Walled in on every side"* → something that distinguishes the cases. **Necessary but not sufficient**, and on its own it is the trap #903 was refused for: a copy-only fix that leaves the mechanism.

**My recommendation: 2 plus 4, and price 3 as a companion.** Option 1 is the architecturally correct one and is the most likely to need an ADR, because it widens a closed requirement vocabulary and would be the first requirement that cannot be checked where the others are.

**Wording is ours** under the owner's 2026-09-04 release of reservation 4; **truth is not waived**, so any sentence must be verified against `traversal.ts` and `enclosure.ts` and quoted verbatim in the commit and pull request body.

## 7. The test that should have caught it, and the mutation

Nothing asserts that a room the game reports complete is **usable**. That assertion is writable and cheap: zone a room, satisfy its object requirements, seal it with no door, and assert that either the readout says so or the need it serves is met. **The surviving mutation to state when this lands:** delete the new reachability signal and watch the assertion go red.

`enclosure.ts`'s docblock proves nobody was careless — the behaviour was understood and written down. **What was missing is a gate on the player-visible consequence**, which is the same shape as #926 (a gate measuring a button's box cannot see a label painting outside it) and #930 (a gate whose unit is an id cannot see an orphan field).

## 8. Weakest claim

**That no player-reachable signal anywhere distinguishes the two rooms.** The run swept the Rooms panel, the roster and the counts channel, and its screen readings are explicitly **upper bounds** — `innerText` does not respect a scroll container's clipping, which that run demonstrated from inside its own control census (21 Build catalogue rows reading `NO BOX` while their labels still appeared in the dump). So a signal in a surface it did not open, or clipped out of a dump, would not have appeared. **What would change it:** a text-node sweep of the assembled page in both prisons, diffed. The behavioural half — hygiene 0% against 96–100% — is a measurement, not an upper bound, and does not depend on this.

Refs #933, #935, #934, #918, #930.
